doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

title: Tom's band on the road: Beaumont, Port Arthur and Thibodeaux
summary: Tom tells about a trip through Louisiana and Texas by Southern Pacific with a band that included Jules Barnes on trombone: a stop with a colored officer in Port Arthur, jobs in Beaumont and Sunday nights in Thibodeaux.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You played carnet in those days I guess. Yeah I was playing carnet.

And this fellow, he used to go, he followed us from, let me see, while we was playing up the road in Long City. And this one used to play high and used to make him high notes there. Yeah. What were you talking about? That Long-Head. Long-Head fellow. Well he followed us way in Beaumont. Oh.

Yvonne. That's right. Well he followed us in Beaumont. And they had a fellow that played piano named Patterson. And his wife used to play together. So we played in Beaumont one night and we played in, what was that place in the back there, Orleans? Port Arthur? Galveston? Port Arthur. Port Arthur. Yeah. But then they had a little train called, in the Irvings. He used to play in some of the things that carried back from Beaumont to Port Arthur. Yeah. And I played over there with him. So I met an officer over there, a colored officer over there, while I was a mason, and me and his mid-friend. So the officer said, well you ain't going back there, let me talk together. He said you ain't going back there with him to Beaumont. So they put him in the, they had a bus, they carried him from the, while we played in Beaumont, in Port Arthur, and carried him to Beaumont. So I stayed with the officer that night. I stayed with the officer that night, and that morning I got up, and I wanted to pay him, oh he wouldn't receive no money, he said, well I was his brother. And we talked at the house there a long time. So I walked all around in, uh, Port Arthur, looking at the different sites, you understand? And I got these in Irvings and come to Beaumont. And he played, they had a talk there, we finished there. I had, I had, Jules Barnes was playing with me then. But we, he used to bring us from here on the, Southern Pacific. We stopped in, uh, Generettes, we stopped in Patterson, we stopped in, uh, Lafayette. Then we went on up to, uh, yeah, we went to Generettes, and from Generettes to Beaumont. After we went to Beaumont, we played in Beaumont that night, and we went on up and, uh, no, I had to come back. That said they were playing in Thibodeau. We was playing every night there in Thibodeau, every Sunday night in Thibodeau. Every Sunday night. So we went on there, it was a night, it took two weeks. And the last night I stopped in Thibodeau and played. And I got here about six o'clock in the morning, uh, with my, I left my, uh, car, I had a truck. I left my truck in Thibodeau. And I caught the fellas, and went on, and I stopped until we played that night, and I come on here. You said, it's Jules Barnes, you say, playing?
Jules was playing trombone. Trombone. Yeah.
He's playing trombone with me then. You remember him? No, I don't. No. I never remember. Al C, little fella they call Dad. You don't look at him.
